title: A map of derived limits induced by a levelwise isomorphism is an isomorphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal D$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], let
$(K_n,f_n)_{n\geq1}$ and $(K'_n,f'_n)_{n\geq1}$ be inverse systems of objects of
$\mathcal D$ whose countable products exist, with derived limits
$K=R\varprojlim_nK_n$ and $K'=R\varprojlim_nK'_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit] given by
Roos triangles $K\to\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nK_n\to K[1]$ and
$K'\to\prod_nK'_n\xrightarrow{1-s'}\prod_nK'_n\to K'[1]$. Let
$(\varphi_n:K_n\to K'_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a morphism of inverse systems
($f'_n\varphi_{n+1}=\varphi_nf_n$) with every $\varphi_n$ an isomorphism, and let
$\varphi:K\to K'$ be a morphism such that $(\varphi,\prod_n\varphi_n,\prod_n\varphi_n)$
is a morphism of the Roos triangles. Then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Stacks Project, Definition 13.34.1 (Tag 08TC) for the Roos triangle and Tag 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle, section Elementary results on triangulated categories) for the five lemma in a triangulated category (a morphism of distinguished triangles two of whose components are isomorphisms is an isomorphism)
